## Figures and framing statistics referenced (not cases)

Electroplated bicycle tube fatality.title: WM_S2014_08
Electroplated bicycle tube fatality.frame: Brief callback ("we talked about electroplating of bicycle tubes") used to anchor the 375°F bake-out rule. If the tube had been baked within an hour of plating, no hydrogen crack would have formed, no fatigue propagation, no paraplegia.

Nautilus submarine hydrogen cracking dur.title: WM_S2014_08
Nautilus submarine hydrogen cracking dur.frame: Centerpiece historical case of the lecture. Mid-1950s Nautilus mockup construction with HY-80; egg-crate stiffener welds made during the day; cracks audible as rifle-shot reports during the night shift — delayed hydrogen cracking, 8-hour diffusion timescale to crack tip. Workaround: switch to austenitic stainless steel electrodes (FCC structure, higher H solubility, lower cracking susceptibility) at the cost of undermatched strength.
Nautilus submarine hydrogen cracking dur.case_name: Nautilus submarine hydrogen cracking during construction

Seawolf submarine welding hydrogen embri.title: WM_S2014_08
Seawolf submarine welding hydrogen embri.frame: One-sentence flag — "I can tell you a story about welding of the Seawolf submarine, and I tracked it down in my opinion to lubricants." Tom does not develop the case here. The hydrocarbon-as-hydrogen-source point is what's being illustrated.
Seawolf submarine welding hydrogen embri.case_name: Seawolf submarine welding hydrogen embrittlement failures

Groton Connecticut submarine welding hyd.title: WM_S2014_08
Groton Connecticut submarine welding hyd.frame: Operational practice case — New London / Groton shipyard electrode-issuance and stub-return protocols. 20 electrodes at a time, 2-hour exposure limit, insulated canisters, mandatory stub return. Also: 85% relative humidity prohibition violated ~200 days/year at east-coast shipyards.
Groton Connecticut submarine welding hyd.case_name: Groton Connecticut submarine welding hydrogen embrittlement failures

ESAB founding from muddy-electrode disco.title: WM_S2014_08
ESAB founding from muddy-electrode disco.frame: Origin story for mineral-coated electrodes. Welder in Gothenburg dipped bar electrode in mud, found mineral coating excluded atmospheric nitrogen and eliminated porosity. Became basis of ESAB, now one of the world's largest welding companies. Also: contemporary discovery of cellulosic coatings from paper-wrapped electrodes.

Henry Bessemer converter development (18.title: MSE_F2016_09
Henry Bessemer converter development (18.frame: Bessemer figures out how to make tons of steel rather than hundreds of pounds; ~10 years of process perfection; the inflection point Tom uses to mark "the Iron Age." Note: a related but distinct entry exists in the canon ("Basic oxygen furnace introduction in Austria"); Bessemer's converter is the prior generation.

Andrew Carnegie and US Steel founding.title: MSE_F2016_09
Andrew Carnegie and US Steel founding.frame: Carnegie scales Bessemer's process to economies of scale, becoming the richest man in the world; sells to JP Morgan for $480M; US Steel later represents the establishment that fails to adopt BOF and continuous casting.

US Steel basic open hearth (early 1970s).title: MSE_F2016_09
US Steel basic open hearth (early 1970s).frame: Tom's central indictment of US Steel management: in the early 1970s, after BOF had been proven for a decade, US Steel built the last large open hearths (450-ton capacity) at ~$1B cost. "Billion-dollar dinosaurs."

Bao Steel government-funded growth.title: MSE_F2016_09
Bao Steel government-funded growth.frame: Current (2016) world's largest steel company; Chinese government funded.

Lakshmi Mittal steel mill acquisition st.title: MSE_F2016_09
Lakshmi Mittal steel mill acquisition st.frame: "They buy plants at ten cents on the dollar when the great managers run them into the ground." Acquired Burns Harbor from bankrupt Bethlehem.

Lakshmi Mittal steel mill acquisition st.title: WM_Su2014_11
Lakshmi Mittal steel mill acquisition st.frame: Mittal buying up distressed steel companies at two cents on the dollar in the late '80s and early '90s; ArcelorMittal as proof that the future-of-metals thesis was right.
Lakshmi Mittal steel mill acquisition st.case_name: Lakshmi Mittal steel mill acquisition strategy

Lakshmi Mittal steel mill acquisition st.title: SMS_F2013_09
Lakshmi Mittal steel mill acquisition st.frame: "This guy in India" bought up unprofitable steel companies for a song; ArcelorMittal became the second largest steel company in the world. Used to illustrate that Wall Street misread steel's productivity-driven margin collapse as industry decline.
Lakshmi Mittal steel mill acquisition st.case_name: Lakshmi Mittal steel mill acquisition strategy

Lakshmi Mittal steel mill acquisition st.title: SMS_F2014_03
Lakshmi Mittal steel mill acquisition st.frame: "Goes around buying up steel companies for a song" — the case that vindicates Tom's "steel isn't dead" thesis against Wall Street and Ned Thomas.

Lakshmi Mittal steel mill acquisition st.title: WIE_F2015_06
Lakshmi Mittal steel mill acquisition st.frame: Mittal recognized in the 1980s that worldwide steel excess capacity was temporary; bought up cheap steel companies (ten cents on the dollar); by 2005 sitting on a fortune as capacity caught up with demand. ArcelorMittal as conglomerate of ~15 pre-1970 firms.
Lakshmi Mittal steel mill acquisition st.case_name: Lakshmi Mittal steel mill acquisition strategy

Lakshmi Mittal steel mill acquisition st.title: MSE_F2017_06
Lakshmi Mittal steel mill acquisition st.frame: Mittal bought distressed steel mills worldwide at ~10¢ on the dollar while Wall Street dumped them; became multi-billionaire as overcapacity worked out. Arcelor Mittal (Luxembourg-based) is the largest European steelmaker; the Thyssen Krupp merger discussion (2017) would make them #2 worldwide after Baosteel.
Lakshmi Mittal steel mill acquisition st.case_name: Lakshmi Mittal steel mill acquisition strategy

Lakshmi Mittal steel mill acquisition st.title: SMS_S2016_04
Lakshmi Mittal steel mill acquisition st.frame: Mittal bought distressed US steel mills at ten cents on the dollar in the late 1980s while Wall Street pronounced steel dead. Used to illustrate the productivity-disguised-as-decline pattern: US steel halved employment 1980–1990 with constant output, doubling productivity at 6–7%/year vs. 1% economy-wide.
Lakshmi Mittal steel mill acquisition st.case_name: Lakshmi Mittal steel mill acquisition strategy

Lakshmi Mittal steel mill acquisition st.title: SMS_S2016_11
Lakshmi Mittal steel mill acquisition st.frame: Closing case. Indian industrialist bought distressed U.S. and European mills at ten cents on the dollar in the 1980s–90s when Wall Street wrote off steel as a dying industry. Became multi-billionaire when overcapacity worked itself out.
Lakshmi Mittal steel mill acquisition st.case_name: Lakshmi Mittal steel mill acquisition strategy

1991 future-of-metals Welding Journal ar.title: WM_Su2014_11
1991 future-of-metals Welding Journal ar.frame: Tom's published argument that metals were not dying, presented against the ceramics/composites/superconductor hype of the late 1980s. Returned to throughout §1 and §2 as the framing device for the productivity argument.

US Steel Price Rollback.title: WM_Su2014_11
US Steel Price Rollback.frame: President Kennedy forces U.S. Steel to roll back a price increase in 1962. Steel-industry executives cite this as the moment they lost profitability; Tom uses it to make the point that steel was the commodity controlling the global economy before the 1973 oil embargo.

MIT basement stainless steel carbon cont.title: WM_Su2014_11
MIT basement stainless steel carbon cont.frame: Low-carbon stainless steel technology invented in the basement of Building 8 in the 1950s; John Chipman as the materials department head (1945–1962) who taught the world how to make reproducible-chemistry steel. The graduate-student-to-industry pipeline that lowered stainless steel costs.
MIT basement stainless steel carbon cont.case_name: MIT basement stainless steel carbon control technology (John Chipman)

Cyril Smith humanities course on materia.title: WM_Su2014_11
Cyril Smith humanities course on materia.frame: Tom's junior-year humanities paper on the hardening of steel, taught by Cyril Smith (former University of Chicago metallurgist who became MIT institute professor in humanities, archaeology of materials).
Cyril Smith humanities course on materia.case_name: Cyril Smith — humanities course on the history of materials

Medieval sword tempering practice.title: WM_Su2014_11
Medieval sword tempering practice.frame: Meteoric iron as the first usable steel; the discovery that hammering, heating, quenching, and tempering produce hardness and ductility. The Crusades-era legend of quenching hot steel by running it through a living slave.
Medieval sword tempering practice.case_name: Damascus sword quenching practice / medieval sword tempering

Eagar manganese deposition expert witnes.title: WM_Su2014_11
Eagar manganese deposition expert witnes.frame: The full arc — sulfur as a 1870s–1880s European problem, Spiegeleisen as the manganese-bearing solution, manganese's essentiality for health, the 1980s–1990s welding-industry litigation, Tom's testimony in Danville, Illinois, the box-of-raisins comparison, the "objection your honor" courtroom moment. Most developed teaching unit in the lecture.
Eagar manganese deposition expert witnes.case_name: Eagar manganese deposition expert witness testimony

Welding industry manganese litigation.title: WM_Su2014_11
Welding industry manganese litigation.frame: The class-action wave against the welding industry on manganese-Parkinson's claims; $100M+ in legal defense costs; the eventual scientific resolution that manganism attacks a different part of the brain than Parkinson's; plaintiffs' attorneys migrating from asbestos to welding.

General Motors Linden New Jersey locatin.title: TQI_S2018_05
General Motors Linden New Jersey locatin.frame: Recap from a prior session. Used as the canonical TPM example — a two-dollar pin that a maintenance engineer never replaced caused several percent scrap. Setup for the broader discussion of acceptable-defect thresholds.
General Motors Linden New Jersey locatin.case_name: General Motors Linden New Jersey locating pin failure

General Motors Linden New Jersey locatin.title: TQI_S2018_06
General Motors Linden New Jersey locatin.frame: Former LFM student Bill Fonte called Tom in to diagnose welding defects at GM's Linden, NJ plant. On-site walkthrough revealed (a) oil contamination preventing electrical ground, (b) a worn hardened-steel locating pin causing fixture slippage, (c) unnecessary galvanizing on an interior hinge causing frosty welds. Each defect was a "hundred dollar bill on the floor" visible to anyone who would walk the line.
General Motors Linden New Jersey locatin.case_name: GM Linden Chevy Blazer — Bill Fonte

Toyota supplier quality crisis (1990s).title: TQI_S2018_05
Toyota supplier quality crisis (1990s).frame: 1990s Columbus, Ohio. A Tier-1 supplier to Honda/GM/Ford/Chrysler arrived 45 minutes late to a dinner because Toyota had summoned him to fix a parts problem same-day. Used to contrast Japanese collaborative supplier management with GM's adversarial "fix it by 9 AM or we sue" approach.
Toyota supplier quality crisis (1990s).case_name: Ohio automotive supplier emergency call from Honda

1973 Honda Civic corrosion failure.title: TQI_S2018_05
1973 Honda Civic corrosion failure.frame: Early 1970s Honda Civics rusting within 12 months of purchase. Used to illustrate Japanese cultural response to quality embarrassment — they were mortified and fixed it, leading to the modern reputation for reliability.

1973 Honda Civic corrosion failure.title: MSE_F2017_04
1973 Honda Civic corrosion failure.frame: Quality-reputation case. Honda's 1973 Civic rusted through in a year; their response built the modern Honda body-engineering reputation.

1973 Honda Civic corrosion failure.title: SSW_S2013_07
1973 Honda Civic corrosion failure.frame: Honda Civics rusting within twelve months in the mid-1970s as origin story for Honda's modern quality culture. "The Japanese don't like to be embarrassed."

Raytheon Aegis missile part aluminum ben.title: TQI_S2018_05
Raytheon Aegis missile part aluminum ben.frame: Early 1980s. A worker straightened a bent aluminum bar with a handheld torch — destroying the heat treatment. Navy inspector caught the lack of procedure, shut down the 400-worker plant. Tom (after Mortensen begged off) called it a tempest in a teapot, wrote up the analysis, and the plant was back in operation by Friday. Used to illustrate Navy SUBSAFE-era documented-procedure enforcement.

Raytheon Aegis missile part aluminum ben.title: CS_F2012_06
Raytheon Aegis missile part aluminum ben.frame: Used to illustrate the role of resident DOD inspectors and the cost of procedure gaps. Navy inspector halts thousand-employee plant for several days; Tom's consulting letter reopens production within 48 hours.
Raytheon Aegis missile part aluminum ben.case_name: Raytheon Aegis missile aluminum welding shutdown

Raytheon Aegis missile part aluminum ben.title: CS_F2012_08
Raytheon Aegis missile part aluminum ben.frame: Illustration of ISO 9000's "everything must have a written procedure" requirement. Navy inspector found a worker putting a torch to heat-treated aluminum with no documented procedure; plant shut down for three days.
Raytheon Aegis missile part aluminum ben.case_name: Raytheon Aegis missile part aluminum bending incident

Upton Sinclair meatpacking industry expo.title: TQI_S2018_05
Upton Sinclair meatpacking industry expo.frame: Brief historical anchor for FDA authority — Upton Sinclair's 1906 book about the meat industry led to the Food and Drug Act. Used to root current FDA Good Manufacturing Practice regulation in a century-old legislative response.
Upton Sinclair meatpacking industry expo.case_name: Upton Sinclair meatpacking industry exposure and Food and Drug Act

Government helicopter design approval an.title: TQI_S2018_05
Government helicopter design approval an.frame: Early 1990s Supreme Court decision (referenced but not named — likely Boyle v. United Technologies). Once the government accepts a contractor's design in writing, the contractor cannot be sued on a design-defect theory. Rationale: cutting-edge defense systems will make mistakes, and Congress chose to absorb that risk. Tom uses this to extend the design-freeze concept from ISO 9000 to defense procurement.
Government helicopter design approval an.case_name: Government helicopter design approval and manufacturer liability protection

Frederick Fish patent attorney (Wright B.frame: Pre-lecture anecdote. Tom did a battery case for Fish & Neave in New York, whose logo features the Wright brothers' glider. Used as conversational opener.

Thixotropic/semi-solid casting patent su.title: CAS_Su2011_05
Thixotropic/semi-solid casting patent su.frame: The rheocast / thixocast / thixomolding family of processes, developed by Flemings' student in 1970, licensed by MIT to a company that sat on it 10–15 years to suppress competition. Modern single-crystal turbine blade cast.case_name: Modern single-crystal turbine blade casting (core shift defect)

NASA deep-space mission plutonium-fueled.title: CAS_Su2011_05
NASA deep-space mission plutonium-fueled.frame: Tom's worked example of why iridium would be the perfect jet-engine material (3000°C melting point) but is impossible at scale (100 oz/year world production). Pivots into the actual deployed application: iridium spheres containing plutonium-238 for RTGs on deep-space probes, with the safety concern that a launch failure scatters nuclear-warhead material into the Atlantic.

NASA deep-space mission plutonium-fueled.title: WM_S2014_01
NASA deep-space mission plutonium-fueled.frame: Used as an example of an exotic welding application (iridium) — about once every 25 years there is a real need to weld iridium spheres around plutonium for deep-space spacecraft RTGs.
NASA deep-space mission plutonium-fueled.case_name: NASA deep-space mission plutonium-fueled thermoelectric generators with iridium containment

US Army M16 firing pin semi-solid steel.title: CAS_Su2011_05
US Army M16 firing pin semi-solid steel.frame: 1970s Army program that gave Flemings' group millions to injection-mold semisolid steel firing pins. Failed because no mold material could withstand the temperatures; 100 parts per $100,000 mold. Used to mark the limit of the semisolid process for steel.
US Army M16 firing pin semi-solid steel.case_name: US Army M16 firing pin semi-solid steel injection molding program

Vancouver World's Fair gold coin.title: CAS_Su2011_05
Vancouver World's Fair gold coin.frame: 36-inch-diameter, 3/4-inch-thick 14-karat gold display coin Tom welded together from cast bars without distortion. ~$4–5M of gold, recovered after the fair.

Reading Pennsylvania copper plant deoxid.title: CAS_Su2011_05
Reading Pennsylvania copper plant deoxid.frame: Green tree trunks thrown into molten copper baths to deoxidize — "poling the bath." Tom proposes (uncertain) that "electrolytic tough pitch" copper's name derives from the pitch resins in the trunk.
Reading Pennsylvania copper plant deoxid.case_name: Reading Pennsylvania copper plant deoxidation process

Continuous casting of steel strip (50-ye.title: CAS_Su2011_05
Continuous casting of steel strip (50-ye.frame: Hazelett's attempt to extend their copper-on-steel-band process to steel strip. Failure mode: steel-on-steel has no thermal conductivity advantage; bands wear out. The "billion-dollar-if-you-solve-it" framing.
Continuous casting of steel strip (50-ye.case_name: Continuous casting of steel strip (50-year unsolved challenge)

Amtrak New Haven to Boston trolley wire.title: CAS_Su2011_05
Amtrak New Haven to Boston trolley wire.frame: Tom's forensic case. British supplier's caster couldn't deliver enough cross-sectional-area reduction; large grains → rough surface → arcing at 100 mph. Tom rejects $6M of wire on two days' notice; British firm sues; counter-investigation by US federal authorities reveals sole-source procurement fraud (Phelps Dodge had been kept out of the bid). Wire is replaced with Phelps Dodge material via the Conform redundant-deformation process. The Providence test-track 6-mile arcing demonstration is the dispositive forensic evidence.
Amtrak New Haven to Boston trolley wire.case_name: Amtrak New Haven to Boston trolley wire / Amtrak catenary wire procurement fraud case

Conform process development.title: CAS_Su2011_05
Conform process development.frame:
Mentioned as the redundant-deformation process Phelps Dodge used to win the replacement contract; also as the process the Army is now evaluating for magnesium armors. British lab origin.

## Cases mentioned in passing

Conform process development.title: CAS_Su2011_06
Conform process development.frame: British severe-plastic-deformation extrusion process from ~30 years ago, in which metal is squeezed through a 90° die at 30× normal extrusion energy, yielding extreme strength and ductility. Tom's Phelps Dodge trolley-wire procurement for the New Hampshire–Boston rail connection used Conform-made wire.

Ingot-cast rim steel surface purity.title: CAS_Su2011_05
Ingot-cast rim steel surface purity.frame: Why ingot-cast rim steel gave the best sheet properties — first stuff to solidify on the mold wall is the purest iron. Used to argue that the casting method has to be chosen for the product (sheet vs. plate).

Generator rotor housing sand casting.title: CAS_Su2011_05
Generator rotor housing sand casting.frame:
4–5-inch-thick cast-iron generator housings the size of a small house — the size-extreme example for sand casting.

1985 Ford Aerostar rear axle fatigue fai.title: WM_Su2014_23
1985 Ford Aerostar rear axle fatigue fai.frame: The shock to Ford when high-strength steel substitution for fuel-economy weight reduction failed in fatigue — Ford's design engineers didn't know what bridge engineers had known for forty years, that welded joints get no fatigue benefit from higher strength steels.
1985 Ford Aerostar rear axle fatigue fai.case_name: 1985 Ford Aerostar rear axle fatigue failures

1985 Ford Aerostar rear axle fatigue fai.title: WM_Su2015_11
1985 Ford Aerostar rear axle fatigue fai.frame: Welded rear axle of HSLA steel, designed assuming fatigue strength proportional to tensile strength. Brackets welded onto axle; field failures in first six months. Big product recall. Triggered industry-wide work on fatigue of welded HSLA sheet.

Cement truck case.title: WM_Su2014_23
Cement truck case.frame: Brief mention. Aluminum water tanks on cement trucks with saddle arrangements — change in stiffness at the saddle creates a fatigue crack location from sloshing liquid.

Caterpillar earthmoving machinery fatigu.title: WM_Su2014_23
Caterpillar earthmoving machinery fatigu.frame: Caterpillar's multi-decade, multi-hundred-million-dollar program to develop welding procedures (torch angle, weave pattern, pulse current, robotic consistency) that produce weld profiles good enough to gain fatigue benefit from higher-strength steels (50 ksi → 60–70 ksi HSLA). Tom consulted briefly; most work is proprietary.

Guthrie weld toe fatigue research.title: WM_Su2014_23
Guthrie weld toe fatigue research.frame: Guthrie's career at the British Welding Institute developing TIG dressing, full-penetration welds, and machined toe profiles to recover the strength-fatigue benefit lost in as-welded fillet joints.

Coast Guard cutter bracket undermatching.title: WM_Su2014_23
Coast Guard cutter bracket undermatching.frame: Brief reference. Undermatching filler metal acceptable here because the brackets had ample weld area, the substrate was high-strength for deflection (not strength) reasons, and undermatching gave better corrosion resistance and toughness.
Coast Guard cutter bracket undermatching.case_name: Coast Guard cutter bracket undermatching case

Navy PH stainless steel hydrofoil rudder.title: WM_Su2014_23
Navy PH stainless steel hydrofoil rudder.frame: Navy used precipitation-hardened stainless on hydrofoil rudders or propellers — high strength, lightweight, 180 ksi. Aluminum hull, PH stainless in the drive end. "We created a few problems back there" — implies a welding consulting episode not developed here.
Navy PH stainless steel hydrofoil rudder.case_name: Navy PH stainless steel hydrofoil components

US Navy superaustenitic submarine materi.title: WM_Su2014_23
US Navy superaustenitic submarine materi.frame: Brief reference. Navy considered replacing HY-100 with super-austenitic stainless (zero ferrite, non-magnetic, no acoustic signature) ten or fifteen years prior. Rejected as overpriced and unnecessary given the threat environment.
US Navy superaustenitic submarine materi.case_name: US Navy superaustenitic submarine material evaluation

Either `Farberware cooking pot thermal w.title: WM_Su2014_23
Either `Farberware cooking pot thermal w.frame: Brief reference. Tom's pot had varying ferrite content from bottom to top — 5–10% ferrite at the bottom, ~80–90% martensite (transformed by deformation) at the top, making the top magnetic. Used to illustrate that "zero ferrite" super-austenitic specifications can be misleading.
Either `Farberware cooking pot thermal w.case_name: Farberware cooking pot thermal warping / stainless steel pot cracking

Miami Art Museum.frame: Setup only — Tom begins the case at the very end of the recording. ~$70M building, ~50 yards from Biscayne Bay, Swiss architect, grand opening planned for the winter donor season. Tom received the call last March. Case body cut off by recording end.

Canadian aluminum-silicon carbide compos.title: SMS_F2013_09
Canadian aluminum-silicon carbide compos.frame: Late 1970s / early 1980s Canadian company that developed a cast aluminum-SiC composite. Canadian aluminum-silicon carbide compos.case_name: Canadian aluminum-silicon carbide composite casting development

University of Alaska asphalt research pr.title: SMS_F2013_09
University of Alaska asphalt research pr.frame: Tom's visit ten or fifteen years before this lecture (so ~late 1990s/early 2000s) to UA Fairbanks, where a program was running on improved asphalts for the southern half of Alaska. Used to illustrate that even mature composite materials (asphalt) have unsolved environmental-durability research problems.
University of Alaska asphalt research pr.case_name: University of Alaska asphalt research program

Alaska highway asphalt degradation.title: SMS_F2013_09
Alaska highway asphalt degradation.frame: North of Fairbanks roads aren't paved because winter freeze-thaw cycles destroy asphalt. Connects to the UA Fairbanks research program above.

Fiberglass truck bed trial at coal mine.title: SMS_F2013_09
Fiberglass truck bed trial at coal mine.frame: Joel Clark, working with Ford, supplied resin-molded composite truck beds to a coal mining operation for a six-month wear test alongside steel beds. The mine refused to return the composite beds because they didn't crack. Used to show composites can win on durability where cost is acceptable.
Fiberglass truck bed trial at coal mine.case_name: Fiberglass truck bed trial at coal mine

Longfellow Bridge guardrail perforation.title: SMS_F2013_09
Longfellow Bridge guardrail perforation.frame: Hundred-year-old Longfellow Bridge handrails are rusted through, perforated, where snow (pH 5.5 frozen acid rain) accumulates and melts. Used to teach atmospheric corrosion rate (~4 mil/year) and the square-root-of-time scaling.

New England highway bridge rebar corrosi.title: SMS_F2013_09
New England highway bridge rebar corrosi.frame: Rebar corrosion expands the steel, blows out concrete, creates highway potholes; full bridge-deck rebuilds required every ~20 years. Used to set up corrosion as steel's Achilles heel and motivate galvanized / stainless / nickel-base rebar substitution attempts.
New England highway bridge rebar corrosi.case_name: New England highway bridge rebar corrosion

Black iron pipe corrosion rate field obs.title: SMS_F2013_09
Black iron pipe corrosion rate field obs.frame: Physical-object demonstration. Tom produces black iron pipe to teach that the magnetite (Fe3O4) scale formed at hot-rolling temperatures adheres to steel because its CTE matches, in contrast to hematite rust which spalls off.
Black iron pipe corrosion rate field obs.case_name: Black iron pipe corrosion rate field observation

Black iron pipe corrosion rate field obs.title: WM_Su2014_05
Black iron pipe corrosion rate field obs.frame: Tom holds up a Home Depot pipe nipple as a physical-object demonstration. Magnetite (Fe₃O₄) coating from mill heat treatment provides practical nobility. Teaching numbers: 0.002–0.010 inches/year corrosion rate; ~25-year shipboard piping lifetime — the historical naval ship life until NAVSEA mandated 50-year lifetime, forcing the move to cupro-nickel, Monel, and titanium.

Steel-toe boot heat treating tank stress.title: SMS_F2013_09

Tank cracked at the welds. Literature said sodium nitrate causes stress corrosion cracking; Tom's U-bend test with anodic polarization wouldn't crack the specimen, but reversing the polarity (cathodic) cracked it within 24 hours. The real mechanism was hydrogen embrittlement, not SCC.

USS Sea Wolf submarine hull cracking.title: SMS_F2013_09
USS Sea Wolf submarine hull cracking.frame: Around 1992 at Groton (Electric Boat), the Navy moved from HY-80 to HY-100 for the Sea Wolf hull. A grinder noticed swarf lining up along sub-eighth-inch cracks in completed welds. Re-inspection found all welds (18% of hull complete) full of microscopic hydrogen cracks. Required scrapping the completed portion, delaying the program a year and costing ~$2 billion. Fix: preheat the steel to 400°F, with welders working in recirculated-liquid blue jelly suits inside heated submarine compartments.

Sylvester wanted to expand into diving and nuclear failure analysis; his prior staff metallurgist had been Dave Holt, a former MIT junior faculty member who'd gone into the ministry after being denied tenure. Bruce Sylvester turned out to be embezzling from his mother's company via fake invoices, caught ~1983; he embezzled half a million dollars and disappeared, leaving his mother to mortgage her home.

MIT engineering department founding chro.frame: Origin of "civil engineering" via 1823 Rensselaer (Erie Canal needs) distinguishing from West Point military engineering. MIT 1865 course numbering: 1 Civil, 2 Mechanical, 3 Mining (→ Metallurgy 1888 → Materials 1974), 4 Architecture, 5 Chemistry, 6 (→ EE 1890s). Elihu Thompson and Edison as GE co-founders. Sloan's 1950 gift removing management from the School of Engineering. Tom's role in the 1996 report creating the Engineering Systems Division — originally drafted as "Division of Engineering Management," renamed to evade Sloan School's M-word ownership. Bioengineering as planned outgrowth of the same perpendicular-structure mechanism.

Pratt & Whitney / General Electric jet e.title: WM_S2014_19
Pratt & Whitney / General Electric jet e.frame: Forensic conclusion. Tom analyzes the 200-ton vessel failure as a three-cause convergence — transient thermal stresses (the operator hadn't waited for thermal equilibration; the design hadn't been modeled in finite element because 1982-era computing couldn't), susceptible microstructure (Japan Steelworks delivered material with toughness below specification, and the un-heated corner regions retained the as-rolled properties), and hydrogen from a corrosion-pit-initiated crack on the water-cooled jacket (the inspection company hadn't been checking the outside often enough; the water treatment company was using out-of-date molybdate chemistry). Critical flaw size: half an inch. Three liable parties: Japan Steelworks, operator, water-treatment / inspection company.

Lead-sealed water pipe failures.frame: Student question prompt. Lead sealing arrived ~1900–1910; Tom has worked on lead-sealed water pipe failures from 90 years out.

Cardiac guide wire lawsuit.title: SSW_S2013_04

Air Force blisk (bladed disc) welding de.title: SSW_S2013_04
Air Force blisk (bladed disc) welding de.frame: 1980s–1990s Air Force program to weld turbine blades directly to disc, eliminating half the rotating mass that lives in the "tree" mechanical attachment. Tried electron beam, laser, arc, linear friction welding. Economics failed at Six Sigma quality requirement.
Air Force blisk (bladed disc) welding de.case_name: Air Force blisk (bladed disc) welding development

Air Force blisk (bladed disc) welding de.title: MSE_F2016_06
Air Force blisk (bladed disc) welding de.frame: "Tens, if not hundreds, of millions of dollars" spent trying to figure out how to weld blades to disk. No commercial product yet at large-engine scale.
Air Force blisk (bladed disc) welding de.case_name: Air Force blisk (bladed disc) welding development

Air Force blisk (bladed disc) welding de.title: SMS_F2014_05
Air Force blisk (bladed disc) welding de.frame: Air Force has spent billions trying to weld blades directly to disc to eliminate Christmas-tree flange weight. 20 lb savings per disc, multiplied by 3–4 discs × 2–4 engines × collateral airframe weight = ~2,000 lb total savings; military aircraft bogey is $1,000/lb saved.
Air Force blisk (bladed disc) welding de.case_name: Air Force blisk (bladed disc) welding development

Pratt & Whitney turbine blade.title: SSW_S2013_04
Pratt & Whitney turbine blade.frame: The physical blade Tom holds up as exemplar of precision-ground "tree" mechanical attachment, Wood's-metal fixturing for the $10M grinding machine. Turbine blade quality control theft risk.title: SSW_S2013_04
Turbine blade quality control theft risk.frame: Tom's anecdote distributing worn/defective Pratt & Whitney blades to ~200 high-school visitors in 1995/96, with care taken about cut-corner and notch markings — at $4,000–$6,000 per blade, defective blades stolen and reinstalled could blow up engines.
Turbine blade quality control theft risk.case_name: Turbine blade quality control theft risk

Percy Bridgeman high-pressure materials.title: SSW_S2013_04
Percy Bridgeman high-pressure materials.frame: Harvard physicist, Nobel laureate, tetrahedral anvil press at gigapascal pressures, foundation for synthetic diamond manufacture. Used to anchor the "parameter" usage dispute with Hallock Campbell.

Percy Bridgeman high-pressure materials.title: DP_S2012_02
Percy Bridgeman high-pressure materials.frame: Extended sketch — Harvard physics professor, Nobel laureate, suicide in Randolph NH 1961. Invented the tetrahedral anvil press, opened up high-pressure materials science (artificial diamond synthesis). Used as the lead-in to the central teaching point: hydrostatic stress suppresses brittle fracture, and at sufficient pressure even steel necks like plasticine. Tom anchors the rock-creep / deep-mine point in Bridgman's framework.

Hallock Campbell AWS definition dispute.title: SSW_S2013_04
Hallock Campbell AWS definition dispute.frame: Hallock Campbell (Harvard grad, AWS glossary author) wrote to Tom in Japan in 1985 critiquing his use of "parameter" in a Welding Journal title. Tom showed the dictionary cited Bridgman; Campbell's handwritten reply: "Percy, how could you?" Used as launchpad for Tom's "weld defined by properties, not process" reformulation in his keynote address.

H.C. Starck Newton tantalum operations.title: SSW_S2013_04
H.C. Starck Newton tantalum operations.frame: H.C. Starck (now part of Bayer) operates one of the world's largest tantalum production facilities in residential Newton, MA. Tom traces its founding to post-WWII MIT mechanical engineering vacuum-melting innovation.

Nuclear Metals Concord depleted uranium.title: SSW_S2013_04
Nuclear Metals Concord depleted uranium.frame: Concord, MA company (now largely defunct) that extruded depleted uranium for bullets, and produced tantalum wire by cold-weld die forging. Tom obtained his tantalum cold-weld sample from them.
Nuclear Metals Concord depleted uranium.case_name: Nuclear Metals Concord depleted uranium extrusion

Kuwait depleted uranium contamination.title: SSW_S2013_04
Kuwait depleted uranium contamination.frame: First Gulf War contamination motivated subsequent Army programs to find tungsten-alloy replacements for depleted uranium kinetic penetrators.

Intel high-power chip thermal management.title: SSW_S2013_04
Intel high-power chip thermal management.frame: Tab-bonded Intel Pentium 1 package with 400 I/O lines (100 per side) used as physical specimen.

WWII ship and tank explosive bonding dis.title: SSW_S2013_04

WWII ship and tank explosive bonding dis.case_name: WWII ship and tank explosive bonding discovery

Coast Guard required Charpy testing at weld centerline, toe, and 1/3/5 mm into HAZ at 20 ft-lb / −20°F. Sparrows Point steel-making struggled to meet the spec on base plate; shipyard would hunt down high-toughness plates (30 ft-lb outliers) to cherry-pick for runoff tab testing — gaming the Coast Guard reporting.
Quincy LNG tanker aluminum tank skirts.case_name: Quincy LNG tanker aluminum tank skirts (Bethlehem Steel A537 development)

Quincy LNG tanker aluminum tank skirts.title: WM_Su2015_05
Quincy LNG tanker aluminum tank skirts.frame: Tom's project welding the steel skirts that supported the aluminum LNG tanks. Coast Guard 20 foot-pound specification at four positions per weld drove the test-plate substitution scheme — the shipyard cut all test plates from the rare 30 foot-pound outlier plate from Sparrows Point.
Quincy LNG tanker aluminum tank skirts.case_name: Quincy Shipyard LNG tanker aluminum tank skirts (Charpy testing)

Tin-bismuth solder steel recycling conta.frame: 25 years prior (~early 1990s) push to replace lead-tin solder with bismuth-tin. Steel industry resistance: 10 ppm bismuth makes steel ingot unrollable (grain-boundary embrittlement, no recovery path except re-mining). Used to illustrate that environmental substitution decisions must consider downstream recycling.

Aluminum can recycling contamination pro.frame: General principle — 6000 vs 5000 series alloy mixing forces downgrading. Turbine blade alloys spec'd virgin-only.

Continuous casting of steel \u2014 Japan.frame: Japanese-led commercialization of continuous casting. Breakouts (shell rupture) catastrophic — hundreds of tons of liquid on a billion-dollar facility, weeks of shutdown.
Continuous casting of steel \u2014 Japan.case_name: Continuous casting of steel — Japanese development

Saugus Ironworks \u2014 energy-crisis em.frame: 1600-era. British wood shortage forced iron production to North America. Tom's estimate: 2,000–4,000 person-hours per ton of steel at Saugus. Today: 15 person-minutes per ton. Tom's headline productivity-gain figure.

Japanese steel manufacturing technology.title: WIE_F2015_06

Japanese steel manufacturing technology.case_name: Japanese steel manufacturing technology — Tom's 1985 Navy-funded visit

Soviet titanium electro-slag welding tec.title: WM_S2014_28
Soviet titanium electro-slag welding tec.frame: Two-pass treatment. First Tom recounts realizing in 1980 that Gurevich's group had used electroslag for the Alpha sub hull. Then he describes returning to MIT and making "probably the first electroslag titanium weld outside of the Soviet Union or France." The Navy classified the result.

Soviet titanium electro-slag welding tec.title: WM_Su2014_33
Soviet titanium electro-slag welding tec.frame: The technical content Tom was after on the exchange. Paton Institute led the world in electroslag, and Tom's group made the first US electroslag weld on titanium ("just in the room next door") after Gurevich quit publishing. Closes with the inference that the Soviets used electroslag to weld their titanium hulls.

Soviet titanium electro-slag welding tec.title: CAS_Su2011_04
Soviet titanium electro-slag welding tec.frame: During a 1980 visit to the Ukraine with Julian Szekely, Tom learned that half of all Soviet steel was electroslag remelted. Julian's interpretation: Soviet BOP steel was so poor (fist-sized inclusions in ship plate) that ESR was necessary just to reach Western BOP quality. The political driver was Dr. Paton at the Paton Institute in Kiev — a WWII hero for electroslag welding of armor plate — who controlled ~25% of Soviet Ukrainian scientific funding and grew his institute to ~5000 people.
Soviet titanium electro-slag welding tec.case_name: Paton Institute and Soviet electroslag dominance

Army helicopter rotor casting weld repai.title: WM_S2014_28
Army helicopter rotor casting weld repai.frame: Tom's student "Gordon" worked at Watertown Arsenal on whether weld repairs of titanium helicopter rotor castings would be acceptable. Result: welds were better than the base metal because of faster cooling and finer Widmanstätten structure. Used to make the point that in titanium, welds can outperform base material in fatigue strength.
Army helicopter rotor casting weld repai.case_name: Army helicopter rotor casting weld repair (early 1980s)

Glomar Explorer (Soviet submarine recove.title: WM_S2014_28
Glomar Explorer (Soviet submarine recove.frame: Howard Hughes's cover for the CIA Glomar Explorer — a multibillion-dollar disguised freighter that lifted a Soviet submarine off the Pacific floor — invoked as the most dramatic example of US deep-sea retrieval capability built up in the same period as the Alvin work.

Beryllium copper spark-free tools (minin.title: WM_S2014_03
Beryllium copper spark-free tools (minin.frame: Tom's own beryllium copper crescent wrench ($130) as a teaching prop. Used in methane-bearing mines because high thermal conductivity prevents the frictional hotspot that would ignite gas. Properties: well over 1 GPa strength, 150–180 ksi, hardness comparable to a steel wrench, but ten times the cost.

HY-80 nuclear submarine steel.title: WM_S2014_03
HY-80 nuclear submarine steel.frame: Used as the canonical example of an alloyed-for-hardenability steel: 1 inch thick, low carbon, ~3% alloy (Ni, Cr, Mo) for through-thickness hardenability in submarine hull plate.

John Wolfe stainless steel sensitization.title: MSE_F2017_06
John Wolfe stainless steel sensitization.frame: Wulff's 1940s patent: deliberately sensitize stainless steel, immerse in nitric acid overnight, dissolve chromium-depleted grain boundaries to produce stainless steel powder. Used pedagogically to show that the same intergranular attack mechanism that makes BWR welds fail is exploited industrially for powder production.
John Wolfe stainless steel sensitization.case_name: John Wulff stainless steel sensitization patent (1940s)

Saudi Arabia gas-reduction steel facilit.title: MSE_F2017_06
Saudi Arabia gas-reduction steel facilit.frame: Saudi natural gas as steel reductant — sidesteps coal-and-coke entirely. Imported iron ore + domestic natural gas + sovereign capital = integrated steelmaking. Part of the road-to-industrialization sequence (steel → ships → autos).

General Motors bankruptcy.title: MSE_F2017_06
General Motors bankruptcy.frame: "They earned it." Parallel to the steel-company bankruptcies of the 1980s. GM's $50 billion plant-and-equipment budget in the 1980s could have bought Toyota outright on the Tokyo exchange. GM bountied robots-for-people while Toyota developed the Toyota Production System.

Conductive polymers / polyacetylene hype.title: SMS_S2016_04
Conductive polymers / polyacetylene hype.frame: A young professor's claim that polyacetylene would replace copper because of higher *specific* electrical conductivity. Tom's shaving-mirror realization the next morning: aluminum already has higher specific conductivity than copper, but we don't use it in rotating machinery — because absolute conductivity is what matters, not specific.

WWII silver-wound magnets from Fort Knox.title: SMS_S2016_04
WWII silver-wound magnets from Fort Knox.frame: Copper shortage during WWII forced Manhattan Project to borrow ~50 tons of silver from the U.S. Mint in Philadelphia for the Calutron magnetic separators at Oak Ridge; returned after the war undamaged.
WWII silver-wound magnets from Fort Knox.case_name: WWII silver-wound magnets from Fort Knox

MIT Building 20 asbestos liability.title: SMS_S2016_04
MIT Building 20 asbestos liability.frame: Tom's role in negotiating the demolition of Building 20 and the development of the Stata Center — proposing that engineering and science compete to raise funds. Engineering raised $115M in 18 months; final Stata Center cost $430M.

Sadoway/Allanore carbon-free metal reduc.title: SMS_S2016_04
Sadoway/Allanore carbon-free metal reduc.frame: Ellingham-diagram thermodynamic argument that any oxide can be reduced by carbon at sufficient temperature, but CO2 externalities are driving MIT research toward electron-based reduction routes.

Charles Martin Hall Niagara Falls Alcoa.title: SMS_S2016_04
Charles Martin Hall Niagara Falls Alcoa.frame: Aluminum smelting is sited at electricity sources — Norway, James Bay, and originally Niagara Falls for Alcoa's first plant.
Charles Martin Hall Niagara Falls Alcoa.case_name: Charles Martin Hall / Niagara Falls aluminum smelting

India cultural gold reserve.title: SMS_S2016_04
India cultural gold reserve.frame: Cultural externality. Half the world's mined gold sits on the necks and wrists of Indian people; cultural color-match drives material demand.

Platinum jewelry in Asia.title: SMS_S2016_04
Platinum jewelry in Asia.frame: Platinum jewelry popular in Asia for color-match with skin tone.

AT&T regulated monopoly and the transist.title: SMS_S2016_04
AT&T regulated monopoly and the transist.frame: Tom's debunking of the basic-research transistor myth. Bell Labs' 1925 statistical projection showed mechanical switch failure rates would collapse the phone system by the 1950s; transistor development was applied research justified within the 6% regulated-profit framework.
AT&T regulated monopoly and the transist.case_name: AT&T regulated monopoly and the transistor

Utility LED light bulb rate-base subsidy.title: SMS_S2016_04
Utility LED light bulb rate-base subsidy.frame: Economic logic of utilities subsidizing efficient bulbs — $2000/kW installed cost of new plants justifies any kWh savings cheaper than that. Massachusetts DPU example.

Cape Wind / Nantucket windmill oppositio.title: SMS_S2016_04
Cape Wind / Nantucket windmill oppositio.frame: NIMBY externality. Residents would oppose tripled electric bills if framed honestly, but frame the objection as aesthetic.

Rhodesian chromite embargo.title: SMS_S2016_04
Rhodesian chromite embargo.frame: Embargo workaround case. Rhodesian chrome ore was uniquely high-grade — crushable directly into a steel furnace for stainless. Embargo was nominally enforced; black-market laundering through third countries was tacitly tolerated by customs.

US copper tubing manufacturing.title: SMS_S2016_04
US copper tubing manufacturing.frame: Transportation externality. Six US copper tubing plants survived 1980s–90s offshoring because the air-in-the-hole shipping cost was prohibitive. Reading Tube as the LGO thesis site.

Bombardier aircraft lightning testing -.title: SMS_S2016_04
Bombardier aircraft lightning testing -.frame: Local-employment externality. Pittsfield MA lightning lab's technicians were barred at the Canadian border; engineers had to perform technician work in-country.
Bombardier aircraft lightning testing -.case_name: Bombardier aircraft lightning testing — Canadian border incident

Norm Augustine socio-engineering 1993 Co.title: SMS_S2016_04
Norm Augustine socio-engineering 1993 Co.frame: Augustine's 1993 University of Colorado engineering centennial talk anticipated the externality-dominated era of materials selection. Posted as course reading.

Mike Ashby materials-over-the-ages plot.title: SMS_S2016_04
Mike Ashby materials-over-the-ages plot.frame: Tom's critique of Ashby's predicted decline of metals and rise of ceramics/composites — argues Ashby bought into 1980s ceramics fever.

Ceramics fever / NIST kitchen-sink talk.title: SMS_S2016_04
Ceramics fever / NIST kitchen-sink talk.frame: Tom's 1986 NIST talk after returning from Japan. Punchline: the only high-volume structural ceramics are portland cement and toilet bowls — "and I throw in the kitchen sink, but you have to line it with gray cast iron." Griffith fracture-mechanics argument: critical flaw size too small to inspect.

Eagar 1991 Welding Journal Future of Met.title: SMS_S2016_04
Eagar 1991 Welding Journal Future of Met.frame: Tom's June 1991 *Welding Journal* article. 95% of world metal is steel; in 1990, steel was a $500B industry at 2% growth — its absolute growth exceeded ceramics ($5B/20%), composites ($15B/10%), and semiconductors ($100B/5%) combined.

Torpedo tube welding distortion control.title: WM_Su2015_11
Torpedo tube welding distortion control.frame: Student-of-Tom anecdote. Balanced-weld procedure (alternating clock positions around the circumference) developed for ~40-foot-long torpedo tubes to control distortion.
Torpedo tube welding distortion control.case_name: John Galati torpedo tube welding (Electric Boat)

Farm equipment engine fire (loose bolt).title: WM_Su2015_11
Farm equipment engine fire (loose bolt).frame: Current consulting case (referenced as "last week"). Bolt-came-loose engine fire on $700k farm equipment, 100 hours old. Defense attorney's theory converts an assembly defect into a design defect via the flatbed-transport argument.

Cement truck pressure vessel explosion (.title: WM_Su2015_11
Cement truck pressure vessel explosion (.frame: Extended teaching case. Aluminum water tank, no doubler plates, regulatory gap (DOT defers to ASME, ASME excludes water tanks, Pennsylvania attorney reads regs and concludes no code applies). Iraq-veteran welder killed during 100 psi over-pressure test repair. Earlier near-miss (leg amputation) had been attributed to a fluke; company responded by building a test cage. Tom got involved through Roger, ex-ASME committee. Hundred thousand similar vehicles on the road; National Board of Pressure Vessel Inspectors says they can't be inspected at that scale.

High-strength truck frame welding violat.title: WM_Su2015_11
High-strength truck frame welding violat.frame: General principle illustration. NHTSA-prohibited welding on HSLA tractor-trailer ladder frames; aftermarket welds cause failure at ~100k miles.

Nautilus submarine hull material (HY-80).title: WM_Su2014_10
Nautilus submarine hull material (HY-80).frame: HY-80 origin story — developed 1940s-50s by U.S. Steel, used in Nautilus, served until "recently being twenty years" on other subs.

Alaska Pipeline construction.title: WM_Su2014_10
Alaska Pipeline construction.frame: Bethlehem Steel in the mid-70s wanted to use a 1% nickel HSLA precursor steel for the Alaskan Pipeline. Would have consumed a substantial fraction of world nickel supply.

US Navy HSLA Steel Mill Investment.title: WM_Su2014_10
US Navy HSLA Steel Mill Investment.frame: Navy developed HSLA-60/80/100 in 1980s-90s for surface ships (more weldable than HY series). Subsequent NAVSEA/Newport News study of HSLA-60 for next-class carrier showed $1/lb material → $10/lb fabricated, killing the weight-saving case.
US Navy HSLA Steel Mill Investment.case_name: US Navy HSLA Steel Mill Investment

Nine-month delayed hydrogen crack (High.title: WM_Su2014_10
Nine-month delayed hydrogen crack (High.frame: Forward-reference — Tom flags a story of hydrogen crack appearing nine months post-weld, attributable to winter freezing trapping the hydrogen. Story itself not delivered in this section.
Nine-month delayed hydrogen crack (High.case_name: Nine-month delayed hydrogen crack (High Sierra mountains)

Nine-month delayed hydrogen crack (High.title: WM_Su2015_06
Nine-month delayed hydrogen crack (High.frame: The exception to the "hydrogen diffuses out within a few days" rule — a weld frozen all winter in the High Sierras retained its hydrogen and cracked the next spring.
Nine-month delayed hydrogen crack (High.case_name: High Sierras nine-month delayed hydrogen crack

Ceramic armor development against shaped.case_name: Ceramic armor development against shaped charges

American Airlines composite rudder separ.case_name: American Airlines composite tail rudder failure (Brooklyn)

Oak Ridge National Laboratory silver mag.title: SMS_F2014_09
Oak Ridge National Laboratory silver mag.frame: Copper was diverted to brass cartridge cases during WWII, so Oak Ridge borrowed ~100 tons of silver from Fort Knox to wind the calutron magnets for uranium isotope separation. Silver returned to Fort Knox after the war.
Oak Ridge National Laboratory silver mag.case_name: Oak Ridge silver magnet windings (Manhattan Project)

MIT conflict of interest in Molten Metal.title: MSE_F2016_05
MIT conflict of interest in Molten Metal.case_name: MIT conflict of interest in Molten Metal promotion

MIT conflict of interest in Molten Metal.title: AM_F2019_03
MIT conflict of interest in Molten Metal.frame: the institutional dimension of the Molten Metal case. John Preston's TLO position; MIT faculty paid $1,000 each on the scientific advisory board not to publicly contradict the technology; VPR declined the conflict-of-interest complaint. Tom explicitly draws the parallel to the contemporaneous Joi Ito / Epstein scandal at MIT.
MIT conflict of interest in Molten Metal.case_name: MIT conflict of interest in Molten Metal promotion

Titusville Pennsylvania - Edwin Drake fi.title: SMS_F2013_01
Titusville Pennsylvania - Edwin Drake fi.frame: Historical anchor for the Oil City story; introduces oil-bubbling-up-from-the-ground geology that becomes the bridge to Alaskan tar sands.

Alaska tar sands and Prudhoe Bay oil see.title: SMS_F2013_01
Alaska tar sands and Prudhoe Bay oil see.frame: Geological externality — how surface oil seeps gave clues to subsurface reserves and produced tar sands as the volatile-stripped residue.
Alaska tar sands and Prudhoe Bay oil see.case_name: Alaska tar sands and Prudhoe Bay oil seeps

Tar sands pond bird kills.title: SMS_F2013_01
Tar sands pond bird kills.frame: Environmental externality with explicit monetized fine ($100,000/bird). Propane cannons as the cost-rational response.
Tar sands pond bird kills.case_name: Fort McMurray tar sands and the Canadian goose fines

Tobacco company metal powder research.title: SMS_F2013_01
Tobacco company metal powder research.frame: Tom's example of how even tobacco research has a material-science angle. Used to illustrate the breadth of externalities and how industry research money flows.
Tobacco company metal powder research.case_name: Nick Grant tobacco company metal-powder consulting

China rare earth embargo on Japan (2010).title: SMS_F2013_01
China rare earth embargo on Japan (2010).frame: Geopolitical externality. Tom uses the embargo to introduce how monopolies are built by undercutting price, then weaponized politically. Sets up the magnet discussion that follows.
China rare earth embargo on Japan (2010).case_name: China rare earth embargo on Japan (2010)

Mountain Pass rare earth mine closure.title: SMS_F2013_01
Mountain Pass rare earth mine closure.frame: U.S. domestic capacity that closed when Chinese prices dropped; reopenable with five-to-ten-year lead time and ~$1B capex.

U.S. Steel 1962 price rollback (Kennedy.title: SMS_F2013_01
U.S. Steel 1962 price rollback (Kennedy.frame: Political externality. Kennedy forced U.S. Steel to roll back prices because steel was the global commodity benchmark and the price rise would have triggered worldwide inflation. Some old-timers blamed this for the industry's decline; Tom blames the 1945 hiring cohort instead.

Bethlehem Steel research labs - 1974 emp.title: SMS_F2013_01
Bethlehem Steel research labs - 1974 emp.frame: Tom's first industry employer. The "1945 cohort" managers who never updated their mindset from 75% world share to 25%. The $600M research facility on South Mountain. Don Blickwede (vice president, MIT MatSci alumnus). Bethlehem's exploration of nuclear steel-making.
Bethlehem Steel research labs - 1974 emp.case_name: Bethlehem Steel research lab and 1974 employment

Norm Augustine aircraft cost projection.title: SMS_F2013_01
Norm Augustine aircraft cost projection.frame: Augustine's log-plot prediction that by 2020 the entire Air Force budget would buy one aircraft; by 2045 the entire DoD budget would buy one. Used as the bridge into externalities-as-a-discipline.

Stout and Doty welding procedure handboo.title: WM_Su2014_13
Stout and Doty welding procedure handboo.case_name: Stout and Doty welding procedure reference

Charlie Brooks textbook martensite cooli.case_name: Charlie Brooks's textbook (martensite nose at 10⁻⁸ seconds)

Quincy Shipyard barge cracking failure.title: WM_Su2014_30
Quincy Shipyard barge cracking failure.frame: Aluminum-cleaning rinse tank maintenance failure. Rinse water pH had drifted to 2.3 (Coca-Cola acidity). Used as cautionary example that chemical-bath cleaning requires maintenance discipline. Barges were destined to carry number six bunker oil.

Quincy Shipyard barge cracking failure.title: WM_Su2014_07
Quincy Shipyard barge cracking failure.frame: Brass heating pipes (3" dia, Dowtherm-heated) inside heavy-crude barges; stress corrosion cracking traced to rinse-water pH of 2.3. Recommendation: change rinse water weekly or daily, with pH monitoring.

Aviation aluminum crankcase weld repair.title: WM_Su2014_30
Aviation aluminum crankcase weld repair.frame: Recent (January 2014) consulting email from a family-owned engine-repair business in Oklahoma, one of the few FAA-approved shops for weld repair of Lycoming and TCM aircraft engine crankcases. The dispute: Canadian failure investigators criticized their use of 4043 filler (undermatching) on Aluminum Association 355 castings. Tom walks through the matching/undermatching/overmatching trade-off and the four classes of filler (4145 overmatching, 4009 matching, 4043 undermatching). Frames the case as a demonstration of how to give a client options without making the design decision yourself ("if an aircraft goes down...I don't want them coming back to me").
Aviation aluminum crankcase weld repair.case_name: Oklahoma aviation engine crankcase weld repair

Ford Explorer chromic acid plating facil.title: WM_Su2014_30
Ford Explorer chromic acid plating facil.frame: Mid-1990s, Ford built an environmentally controlled chromic acid plating shop for Ford Explorers at a couple hundred million dollars. Used to mark the end of the chrome-plating gap that began in 1982.
Ford Explorer chromic acid plating facil.case_name: Ford Explorer chromic acid plating shop

Historical water conveyance material evo.title: MSE_F2016_07
Historical water conveyance material evo.frame: Survey of water pipe material substitutions from 4000 BC clay pipes through Roman aqueducts, wood, cast iron / ductile iron, and into polymer transitions. Used to set up the embrittlement issue with century-old cast iron mains.
Historical water conveyance material evo.case_name: Historical water conveyance — clay to ductile iron

HDPE pipe fracture on Hudson River barge.title: MSE_F2016_07
HDPE pipe fracture on Hudson River barge.frame: Holman's own consulting case. Thousands of feet of HDPE pipe fusion-welded on a barge and pulled under the Hudson; one fracture investigated. Used to introduce fusion-welded polymer pipe and the open question of century-scale durability.
HDPE pipe fracture on Hudson River barge.case_name: HDPE gas pipe fracture on Hudson River barge

Samsung Galaxy Note 7 thermal runaway re.title: MSE_F2016_07
Samsung Galaxy Note 7 thermal runaway re.frame: Student raises the iPhone 7 / Note 7 fires; Holman uses it to introduce battery thermal runaway and Samsung's 60% charge-cap response.

Vape pen battery spontaneous ignition.title: MSE_F2016_07
Vape pen battery spontaneous ignition.frame: Holman cites his own consulting work on vape pen fires as a class of cases parallel to phone-battery fires.

Skyscraper glass curtain wall panel brea.title: MSE_F2016_07
Skyscraper glass curtain wall panel brea.frame: Holman's consulting work on structural glass failures in curtain walls. IGU optimization shrunk the gap layer, raised internal temperatures under morning sun, produced thermal stress breakage. Notes the LEED-credit trade-off.
Skyscraper glass curtain wall panel brea.case_name: Skyscraper IGU thermal stress glass breakage

Crane rail forging burst failure.title: MSE_F2016_07
Crane rail forging burst failure.frame: Holman's consulting case. Crane rail on a dredging barge turntable fractured; sectioning revealed an internal forging burst from refractory inclusion during manufacture. Should have been caught by pre-service ultrasonic inspection. Holman passes the sectioned sample around the class.

Container ship wire rope fracture.title: MSE_F2016_07
Container ship wire rope fracture.frame: Holman's consulting case on a fractured cargo-container lifting rope. Full-scale tensile test in a three-story vertical machine; broke above 300,000 lb (Holman conflates with ksi in delivery — see editorial register flag).

Lehigh University five-million-pound str.title: MSE_F2016_07
Lehigh University five-million-pound str.frame: Cited as the largest tensile/structural test facility Holman has seen; full-scale bridge section testing to failure. Used to make the cost argument for computer simulation.
Lehigh University five-million-pound str.case_name: Lehigh University full-scale bridge test facility

Navy topside weight reduction composite.title: MSE_F2016_07
Navy topside weight reduction composite.frame: Holman's master's thesis work. Open- and closed-cell aluminum foam sandwich structures, dip-brazed in molten sodium fluoride, evaluated as topside-weight alternatives to monolithic aluminum. Holman shows samples. Discusses maintainability barrier to field deployment.
Navy topside weight reduction composite.case_name: Navy topside weight reduction — aluminum foam sandwich structures

Miami Art Museum hanging garden failure.title: WM_Su2014_24
Miami Art Museum hanging garden failure.frame: Forensic consulting case (Tom retained by general contractor). 20-ton reinforced concrete cantilevered beams in a Miami building, hung by two three-quarter-inch threaded rods in tension, originally specified in 410 martensitic stainless. Tack welds caused delayed hydrogen cracking; beams fell in August and November 2012. Material substitution to 316 austenitic stainless raised chloride stress corrosion cracking concerns at the marine site; Tom refused to sign off as PE, sent a written notice to general contractor, who forwarded it to the owner. Final resolution: duplex stainless steel. Litigation pending as of recording (Summer 2014).
Miami Art Museum hanging garden failure.case_name: Miami Art Museum hanging garden failure

Miami Art Museum hanging garden failure.title: COR_Su2016_02
Miami Art Museum hanging garden failure.frame: Six-story hanging garden 100 yards from Biscayne Bay. 410 martensitic stainless steel tension bolts failed during construction (low fracture toughness + tack welds). 316 proposed; Tom warned of SCC. Settled on 2205 duplex (Sandvik recommendation), no weld details. Cost increase 7–8M on a 60M building. Tom refused to sign off as engineer of record. Used to teach martensitic vs duplex stainless steels, stress corrosion cracking, and consulting liability.
Miami Art Museum hanging garden failure.case_name: Miami Art Museum hanging garden failure

Tom Eagar's residential high-efficiency.title: WM_Su2014_24
Tom Eagar's residential high-efficiency.frame: Personal anecdote, late 1970s. Tom declined to pay $2,000–$3,000 to line his chimney stack with superferritic stainless steel to route boiler exhaust up the stack rather than out the side wall; still vents through the side decades later. Used to illustrate the superferritic / chloride-cracking-resistance application and the role of mortgage-scale economics in materials selection at the consumer level.
Tom Eagar's residential high-efficiency.case_name: Tom Eagar's residential high-efficiency boiler chimney

Oil refinery pipe lot rejection.title: CS_F2012_12
Oil refinery pipe lot rejection.frame: Brief reference. One leaky pipe out of 600 led purchaser to condemn entire lot and demand refund. Tom characterizes this as "not the appropriate way to handle that problem." Used to contrast statistical reality of NDT with overreaction to single failures.

Allegheny River interstate highway bridg.title: CS_F2012_12
Allegheny River interstate highway bridg.frame: Tugboat captain noticed a crack in an interstate highway bridge over the Allegheny in Pittsburgh growing between trips. By the time inspectors reached it, the crack was nine feet long and visible from 20-30 feet. Used to illustrate: (1) why pressure vessel safety factors exceed bridge/building safety factors (consequences of failure), (2) redundancy in bridge structures.
Allegheny River interstate highway bridg.case_name: Allegheny River interstate highway bridge crack

X-33 hydrogen tank adhesive joint failur.title: CS_F2012_12
X-33 hydrogen tank adhesive joint failur.frame: Composite hydrogen tank originally designed for 2.0 safety factor. Manufacturing defects (potentially 3-4 inches in size) led program to recalculate as 1.05 safety factor to justify proceeding to test rather than scrapping $225M-$250M vessels. Failed in test at Huntsville. Used as exemplar of "political games" with safety factors.

X-33 hydrogen tank adhesive joint failur.title: SMS_S2016_01
X-33 hydrogen tank adhesive joint failur.frame: A piece of the X-33 hydrogen tank is shown as an example of a $12,000/lb fabricated structural material. Used as the high-end anchor of the price-per-pound argument that becomes §8. No failure discussion here.

X-33 hydrogen tank adhesive joint failur.title: SMS_S2016_06
X-33 hydrogen tank adhesive joint failur.frame: Half-size shuttle-replacement prototype. Adhesively bonded hydrogen tanks at $250M each, factor-of-safety reduced from 2.0 to 1.05 to meet schedule. Held during cryogenic test, failed on warm-up. $1.3B program cancellation.

X-33 hydrogen tank adhesive joint failur.title: SSW_S2013_02
X-33 hydrogen tank adhesive joint failur.frame: Two adhesively-bonded Nomex/carbon-fiber composite liquid hydrogen tanks built at $50 million apiece, ~4,000 pounds each, ~$12,000/lb fabrication cost. "Except it didn't [work]. But that's another story." Physical sample passed around class.
X-33 hydrogen tank adhesive joint failur.case_name: X-33 space plane composite hydrogen tank

1988 Northeast snowstorm building collap.title: CS_F2012_12
1988 Northeast snowstorm building collap.frame: Storm of the century, through Princeton NJ and eastern Pennsylvania. Prefabricated buildings with computer-optimized roof joists (designed to 1.67 minimum rather than the historical 2.0+ rule-of-thumb) collapsed under snow loads. Cause: optimization had eaten the implicit safety margin that had previously made 1.67 effectively higher.

1906 San Francisco earthquake and fire.title: CS_F2012_12
1906 San Francisco earthquake and fire.frame: Tom misdates as "1912 or whatever." Triggered modern building codes for earthquake protection in the U.S.

Oakland Bay Bridge 1989 Loma Prieta part.title: CS_F2012_12
Oakland Bay Bridge 1989 Loma Prieta part.frame: Tom mentions a section collapsed but doesn't recall fatalities. Brief reference; not developed.

Nova Scotia sailboat trailer weld failur.title: CS_F2012_11
Nova Scotia sailboat trailer weld failur.frame: Tom's forensic case. A farmer-built sailboat trailer with a slugged weld (bolt buried in the joint, then welded over) fractured on Route 24 south of Boston on the return trip from a Newport race, destroying the 40-foot sailboat. Used to illustrate why standards prohibit welding on tractor-trailer frames and what "slugging a weld" means.
Nova Scotia sailboat trailer weld failur.case_name: Nova Scotia sailboat trailer weld failure

Jet engine removal bolt design failure.title: CS_F2012_11
Jet engine removal bolt design failure.frame: Stage-business case. Tom passes around a hardened steel bolt assembly used to dismount jet engines from aircraft wings. The bolt had two diameters with flats on the center shoulder for restraint; mechanics torqued only the outer nut, ignoring the shoulder, which over-torqued the assembly and initiated a crack. A 5-million-dollar engine dropped on the tarmac. Used to introduce load-path reasoning.
Jet engine removal bolt design failure.case_name: Jet engine removal bolt design failure

Stata Center (Frank Gehry conceptual des.title: CS_F2012_11
Stata Center (Frank Gehry conceptual des.frame: Stage-business case. Tom crumples four sheets of paper to demonstrate how Frank Gehry presented the conceptual design of the Stata Center to MIT physical-plant head Vicki Sirianni. Budget went from $115M to $430M; MIT froze salaries for two years. Used to illustrate how informal conceptual designs become consequential.
Stata Center (Frank Gehry conceptual des.case_name: Stata Center (MIT Building 32 / Gehry crumpled-paper concept)

Chevrolet Vega engine removal for spark.title: CS_F2012_11
Chevrolet Vega engine removal for spark.frame: Brief design-foible aside in the Hyatt section. The 1978 Chevy Vega had to have its engine removed to change spark plugs because surrounding components blocked wrench access. Used as a low-stakes illustration of the same as-designed / as-serviceable gap.
Chevrolet Vega engine removal for spark.case_name: Chevy Vega engine removal for spark plug service

General Motors sliding door van lemon-la.title: CS_F2012_11
General Motors sliding door van lemon-la.frame: Personal forensic case, 1985. The sliding side door of Tom's GM van fell off five times. After a nasty letter from the dealership owner, Tom filed lemon-law demand; GM offered an executive vehicle, then offered cash instead when the executive's loaner wasn't ready. Used as a narrative bridge into the Taurus case and to illustrate manufacturer response patterns.
General Motors sliding door van lemon-la.case_name: General Motors sliding-door van lemon-law case

Bethlehem Steel looper program and Lacka.title: MSE_F2016_11
Bethlehem Steel looper program and Lacka.frame: Tom's 20-month tenure at Bethlehem Steel, 1975. The looper rotation program (Martin Tower vice-presidential lectures). The Lackawanna 1910/1911 coke ovens "fully depreciated, costs us nothing" misconception. The MIT-PhD boss / Lehigh-PhD manager who vetoed a no-cost quality improvement. The Homer Research Labs executive dining room with tennis-ball-sized strawberries. Six of the top ten paid US executives at Bethlehem in the 1930s while the company was losing money. Eugene Grace's tonnage-based compensation. Gulfstream jets to Florida.
Bethlehem Steel looper program and Lacka.case_name: Bethlehem Steel looper program and Lackawanna depreciation case

Boeing door product center manufacturing.title: MSE_F2016_11
Boeing door product center manufacturing.frame: mid-1990s plant tour. Deterministic manufacturing (orders three years out, doors one year out). Seven drillings per rivet hole. 750 doors, 250 employees → $50,000/door by the $100k-per-employee rule. Today probably a $100k door.

Corning Willow Glass development.title: MSE_F2016_11
Corning Willow Glass development.frame: 100–200 micron alkali-free borosilicate glass sheet, ~2014 release. Tom's inference: must be a laminated three-layer structure (like Corning Ware) with mismatched-CTE middle layer keeping surfaces in compression. Architectural backsplash application.

England 16th century 17th century defore.title: SMS_S2016_11
England 16th century 17th century defore.frame: The structural argument for why American iron industry began — England exhausted its forests for charcoal (iron, shipbuilding, glass) and forced colonial relocation.
England 16th century 17th century defore.case_name: England 16th-17th century deforestation and energy crisis

Allegheny Ludlum AOD Bearing Failure.title: SMS_S2016_11
Allegheny Ludlum AOD Bearing Failure.frame: Tom's consulting visit for an AOD-vessel bearing failure. Used as the occasion to observe hourly workers' regard for Dick Simmons.

Andrew Carnegie and Eagar grandfather Un.title: SMS_S2016_11
Andrew Carnegie and Eagar grandfather Un.frame: Tom's grandfather (former mayor of Chattanooga) sought $25,000 from Carnegie to complete a $500K matching grant (Rockefeller's $250K) for the University of Chattanooga. Carnegie asked his education level; grandfather said 13 months; Carnegie revealed he too had 13 months and granted the funds. The anecdote serves as a Carnegie character study and a generational bridge to the steel-industry narrative.

Dick Simmons private plane story.title: SMS_S2016_11
Dick Simmons private plane story.frame: Tom drove Simmons to "the airport"; only at general aviation did Simmons sheepishly admit he owned his own plane. Used to characterize Simmons's personal modesty against his financial scale.

America's Cup hydraulic cylinder stress.title: WM_Su2015_15
America's Cup hydraulic cylinder stress.frame: Worked fracture-mechanics example. 7075-T6 piston cylinder in a yacht winch hydraulic system, operating at 7,500 psi, failed by stress corrosion cracking from saltwater exposure. Critical flaw size calculation showed ~1 mm — confirmed by examination of the fracture surface. Solution: switch to 7075-T73 (over-aged, lower yield, higher toughness and corrosion resistance) with slightly thicker wall, achieving leak-before-break.
America's Cup hydraulic cylinder stress.case_name: America's Cup hydraulic cylinder stress corrosion cracking (Navtech consulting case)

Wright brothers' aircraft engine precipi.title: WM_Su2015_15
Wright brothers' aircraft engine precipi.frame: Brief teaching aside on natural aging. SEM study of the engine block in the Smithsonian showed aluminum-copper precipitates still coarsening after a hundred years at room temperature; data fell on a straight line on a log-time scale.
Wright brothers' aircraft engine precipi.case_name: Wright brothers' aircraft engine precipitate coarsening (Smithsonian study)

Aluminum-lithium development for Space S.title: WM_Su2015_15
Aluminum-lithium development for Space S.frame: Thirty-year development arc. Soviets discovered aluminum-lithium alloys in the 1970s. Alcoa worked on it for thirty years through hot cracking and weldability problems. Used at the end of the Space Shuttle main tank lifetime and in Boeing 787 components. Lithium reduces density 10%, raises Young's modulus 10%, giving 20% improvement in E/ρ. Still difficult to weld, and lithium worsens corrosion.
Aluminum-lithium development for Space S.case_name: Aluminum-lithium development for Space Shuttle and Boeing 787

Washington Monument aluminum apex.title: WM_Su2015_15
Washington Monument aluminum apex.frame: Brief historical anecdote — aluminum pyramid at the top of the Washington Monument as a lightning rod, made of aluminum because at the time (1880s) it was more valuable than gold.

Hall-H\u00e9roult aluminum refining disc.title: WM_Su2015_15
Hall-H\u00e9roult aluminum refining disc.frame: Simultaneous independent invention by Charles Martin Hall (founder of Alcoa) and Paul Héroult of France, within two months of each other and with no communication. This is the foundational moment for cheap aluminum.

Novelis Skooter co-cast Alclad process.title: WM_Su2015_15
Novelis Skooter co-cast Alclad process.frame: Modern Alclad manufacture. Traditional roll-bonding of pure-aluminum cladding onto a high-strength aluminum-alloy core had ~15% yield. Novelis (Alcan/Péchiney merger entity) developed co-casting that gives ~100% yield. Outside skin of Airbus aircraft is Alclad of this type.

(2) The plasma-sprayed inner surface for Teflon adhesion introduced hydrogen (95% argon / 5% hydrogen gas), which caused delayed cracking after shipping from Brooklyn to Japan. Martensite transformation in deformed 304 stainless was the susceptible microstructure.

Corrugated stainless steel tubing (CSST).title: CS_Su2012_07
Corrugated stainless steel tubing (CSST).frame: The lecture's summative case. The 2003 Arkansas class action settled; one Texas county banned the product. ## Figures referenced (recurring numeric anchors, not cases)

- Steel labor content: 50% in Tom's early career → 5% today (§1.p7).
- 1980s steel industry productivity growth: 4% per year; manufacturing 2%; services 0% (§1.p8).
- 1980s mining productivity growth: 7% per year; compounded over 20 years = 20× improvement (§1.p9).
- Material cost as fraction of total product cost: ~10% (§9.p1) — restated from prior lecture.
- DOE magnesium-in-automobiles research spend: ~$100 million per year for forty or fifty years (§5.p1).
- Commercial jetliner lifetime: ~100,000 flight hours (§7.p2).
- H₂O electrochemical breakdown: ~1.1 V (§8.p3).
- Al₂O₃ / MgO decomposition: <2 V, probably <1.5 V (§8.p4).
- Primary bond energy: 1–3 eV (§8.p5, §11.p9).
- Energy/wavelength relation: E (eV) = 12,400 / λ (Å) = 1.24 / λ (μm) (§11.p10).
- UV cutoff: <0.310 μm → ~4 eV (§11.p11).
- Atmospheric CO₂: ~300 ppm; zinc carbonate formation timescale: ~1 year (§9.p9).
- Magnesium anode purity spec: <7 ppm nickel (§4.p9).
